contract_assessment.assessment: SecretKey, WordIndexes, private SessionSeedWordIndexes and SessionKeySource have fixed redacted Debug, private material fields and no Clone/Copy. SecretKey intake clears its mutable input on success and failure. Public conversion/export outputs remain deliberate caller-owned codec boundaries. From-slice index construction can hold invalid shape/range, but retained source insertion checks shape/range/checksum; invalid public input cannot bypass add_bip39_seed/add_source.

Insertion consumes secret owners; take_last transfers with mem::take and constructors no longer clone out of the eight-slot temporary. Source validity and capacity are checked before retained mutation. Import consumes pending source even on rejection/error; transcript capacity is checked before add_source. Independent decision-step overflow specifically returned Capacity without loading a source. Existing keyring entries survived exhaustive invalid inserts and full-ring import failure.

Raw payload construction is crate-private; fields are private and reveal methods explicitly borrow for trusted local output. Payload exists as a wiping owner before fallible construction fills it. Non-IO flow returns one payload after its legacy approval decision; IO borrows for emission and returns no retained payload. Source/payload/nested flow Debug do not reveal material. Simulator backup mismatch diagnostics no longer echo secret encodings. This is memory/API hygiene, not a physical approval boundary.

Owned scalar/index/payload storage, decode/checksum buffers, fingerprint material and current SHA core/block buffer have maintained zeroization. The enabled SHA zeroize feature reaches digest and block-buffer; the public adapter exposes no Debug/Clone/serialization. Small arithmetic/encoding temporaries, Rust moves/registers and backend scratch are not claimed erased. Caller input/output, display/camera storage and labels remain explicitly allocated/cleared by their owners. No safe Rust post-drop memory read was used as proof.

Product pins zeroize 1.9.1 without defaults and sha2 0.11.0 without defaults with zeroize. Archive digests match lock/checksum manifests and retained vendor bytes/notices; live crates.io confirms direct pins are non-yanked with matching checksums. RISC-V feature closure has no allocator, std or entropy dependency. The small adapter delegates SHA256 and preserves the existing known-answer/streaming contract. Targeted source inspection confirms SHA core and buffer Drop behavior; no whole-backend erasure claim follows.

k256 0.14.0 with schnorr/ecdh and the secp256k1 0.33.1/sys 0.14.1 lowmemory alternative are confined to the existing feasibility probe. Raw sign_raw/verify_raw and libsecp raw signing use the intended message directly. Both ECDH wrappers use shared x before HKDF extract with nip44-v2. Fresh independent rerun passed every pinned official oracle plus wrong-prehash and hashed-ECDH negatives. Candidate selection is reasonable for later integration, subject to target timing and secret scratch obligations. Full NIP44 encryption is not claimed.

No production random provider or signer was added. Legacy generate functions are documented deterministic conversion. The entropy contract requires fallible whole-buffer fill, wiping partial failures, bounded scalar rejection, no unqualified fallback and source/FFI/weak-symbol/runtime/final-binary tracing plus actual invocation/fault tests per device. Qualified OS CSPRNG/DRBG is permitted. Statistical tests or this ISA link do not qualify entropy or select an ESP32 assembly. No source audit or successful link is substituted for physical evidence.

acceptance_review.basis: Reviewed complete material-bearing APIs and consumer diff; reran all 11 external compile-fail doctests. Author redaction/IO/error tests and baseline exposure logs hash-verified. Explicit codecs remain allowed exports; stored source fields cannot be accessed externally.

Secret-flow inventory matches source and bounded fixed-array ownership. Independent state/transfer/error experiments pass. Current storage cleanup is distinguished from old move/compiler/register copies; device placement/internal RAM remains a later obligation.

Maintained package versions/licenses/features/source provenance checked; official vectors rerun; author ARM/RISC-V compile/link records reconciled. Independent actual-core RISC-V final link has no undefined symbols and exactly reproduces the author ELF SHA256. No physical or peak-memory claim.

Independent rerun yields 19 BIP340 verification and 8 exact signing cases per backend, 43 NIP44 conversation cases per backend, and both integration trap negatives. Preserved C ABI failure is the expected different floating-point ABI error; corrected command pins clang and -mabi=ilp32f -march=rv32imafc.

Entropy contract explicitly covers failure/partial/stuck/interrupted source, no fallback, FFI/weak/runtime provenance and actual device invocation. Source/feature inspection agrees that no production provider exists, so no runtime entropy quality is claimed.

independent_adversarial_experiment.hypothesis: Owned seed insertion might skip or miscompute checksums, corrupt existing slots on failure, or import before a final transcript-capacity error. Test against a separately computed oracle and adversarial state boundaries.
independent_adversarial_experiment.design: Python integer assembly of ENT||CS plus hashlib/OpenSSL constructs all 2048 possible final words for 12/15/18/21/24-word lists whose preceding indexes are zero. External Rust crate calls only public candidate APIs; it does not use candidate checksum outputs as the oracle. Every insertion is checked against the oracle and an already retained scalar fingerprint, then valid sources are moved/reinserted. Supported backups are checked against independently reconstructed entropy/digits. Separate tests exercise full-ring insertion, the 33rd-button approval when transcript capacity is 32, and exact scalar-order boundary.

result.scalar_boundary: n-1 accepted; n and n+1 rejected; mutable inputs all zero afterward

independent_adversarial_experiment.limits: Synthetic public low-entropy fixtures; no entropy-quality, physical-erasure, constant-time or exhaustive arbitrary mnemonic claim.

nonblocking_observations.observation: A caller can supply approval buttons through the existing public non-IO flow. API opacity is not an authority boundary inside the trusted image. The brief and handoff explicitly defer physical-origin, one-use authorization repair; this review does not qualify that behavior.

k256 SigningKey Drop wipes its key but sign_raw nonce derivation arrays and NonZeroScalar temporaries lack universal Drop wiping; C bindings have explicit copy/erase limits too. These are documented, not silently accepted as full erasure. Real-key admission must resolve relevant scratch and target timing/memory requirements.

Historical crypto providers reuse ELF output paths, so earlier provider ELFs are overwritten. Saved logs, commands and declared hashes are intact, but I cannot rehash every older binary from retained bytes. Preserve per-provider/per-target ELFs in isolated named artifact locations for later binary audits. This does not invalidate inspected source/vector/link-log evidence; actual core ELF was independently rebuilt to the exact declared hash.
